brief.outcome: Launch a podcast for the owner's coaching business for engineers moving into management within eight weeks, and have it bring at least 4 discovery calls a month within six months of launch.
brief.deliverable: A launched podcast: a chosen format and name, cover art, a trailer and the first episodes recorded and edited, the show live on the main podcast apps, a listener page with a booking link, and a way to tell which calls came from the podcast, all inside the budget, with a monthly readout of calls.
done: Baseline of discovery calls a month and how callers found the owner, read from Calendly
Format (interview, solo or mix) chosen by the owner from costed options
Show name, description, cover art and a trailer ready and approved
At least the launch episodes recorded and edited without the owner needing editing skills
Show live on the major podcast apps, with a page and booking link that records where callers came from
Calls from the podcast counted each month against 4 a month
Learnings saved for the next season

metric.name: Discovery calls a month that came from the podcast

brief.deadline: Launch within eight weeks (about 28 December 2026); 4 calls a month within six months of starting (about May 2027)
guardrails: Spend stays within $1,500 for setup and $200 a month after
The owner's existing LinkedIn audience and email list are not spammed: promotion is spread out and unsubscribes are watched
Episodes are published on a schedule the owner can keep
Calls from other sources are not neglected or double counted as podcast calls

The owner has a decent microphone, so no new microphone is bought unless the owner agrees
The owner has no editing skills, so editing is done by a tool or an outside editor within budget

research.approach: Practitioners launching a podcast to win clients work backwards from the call: they name one listener and the problem that listener has, choose a format they can keep up, and decide the call to action before recording. They launch with a trailer and at least two or three episodes ready so a new listener can binge, host the audio with a service that makes the RSS feed, and submit that feed to Apple Podcasts and Spotify. They build a page for the show with a clear route to booking, and they measure calls by asking callers how they found them as well as counting downloads, because downloads alone do not show business. A solo-led or coaching-style show is the usual choice for lead generation, with interviews used when guests bring a real audience. Editing is either learned, done by a tool, or bought, and is planned before recording starts.

sources.title: Starting a podcast checklist (HubSpot)
sources.note: Order: niche, ideal listener, name, format and schedule, host, cover art, equipment, outline 10 to 20 episodes, record three, show notes, trailer, upload, submit, market. Pick a schedule you can keep.

sources.title: Apple Podcasts requirements (Apple Podcasts for Creators)
sources.note: Public RSS 2.0 feed, artwork, at least one episode, stable episode IDs. Page is undated; read 2026-11.

sources.title: Podcast strategy for lead generation (Sproutworth)
sources.note: Choose a format for strengths and audience, put calls to action at the start, middle and end, track which episodes drive leads. The page shows 2024-08-15 and 2026-10-13; the later is taken as the update. A marketing blog, so guidance not evidence.

steps.name: Find today's discovery-call baseline and how callers find the owner
steps.why: Without a baseline the podcast's calls cannot be told from other sources.

steps.name: Define the listener and what they need from the show
steps.why: Every launch checklist starts with one listener and one problem.

steps.name: Study comparable shows for format, length and cadence
steps.why: Shows the owner's listeners already hear and what is missing.

steps.name: Choose format, host and editing route within budget
steps.why: Format and editing are the decisions the owner is unsure about and the budget limits them.

steps.name: Design the show: name, cover, trailer, first episodes and the call to action
steps.why: The call to action and the first episodes are set before recording.

steps.name: Record, edit and write show notes for the launch episodes
steps.why: Launching with a few episodes ready lets new listeners binge.

steps.name: Build the listener page, booking route and call tracking
steps.why: A clear route to the booking link and a how-did-you-hear question make calls countable.

steps.name: Submit the feed and launch with promotion spread over weeks
steps.why: Directories need a valid feed and one episode; promotion drives the first listeners.

steps.name: Count calls and downloads monthly and adjust
steps.why: Leads, not downloads, are the goal; find which episodes bring calls.

pitfalls.text: Recording before the listener, format and call to action are decided.
Launching with one episode, or with no way to submit because the feed is invalid.
Counting downloads as success when no booking is traced to the show.
A format the owner cannot keep up weekly, so the show stops after a few episodes.
Weak or hidden calls to action, so listeners enjoy the show but never book.

stages.name: Pin down the goal, budget and limits
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured goal, a budget, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Read the discovery-call baseline
stages.goal: Count discovery calls a month and any source answers from Calendly for the last six months.

checks.name: Calls are counted per month for six months, or the gap is stated
States how many callers said how they found the owner, and that the rest is unknown
No booker names or emails are copied into project files

stages.name: Define the listener and what they need
stages.goal: From the owner's top posts, replies and call questions, write one listener profile and the five questions they ask most.

checks.name: Each question traces to a post, reply or call theme the owner gave
One listener and one core problem, not a list of everyone
Guesses are marked as assumptions to test

stages.name: Study comparable shows
stages.goal: List career and management shows for engineers or technical people: format, episode length, cadence, call to action and what is missing.

checks.name: At least five shows, with when each was read
States what no comparable show does that this one could
No download or revenue figures are quoted unless a source gives them

stages.name: Check the baseline can be trusted
stages.goal: Check the call counts and what the booking page records today, and say whether a podcast call can be told apart.

checks.name: Rescheduled and cancelled bookings are not counted as new calls
States whether Calendly records a source today and what must be added
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for judging 4 calls a month

stages.name: Cost the format, host and editing options
stages.goal: Build two or three complete options (solo, interview, mix; host; editing route) each with launch cost, monthly cost, weekly owner hours, risk and how it will be measured. Show which fit $1,500 and $200 a month.

checks.name: Every option shows setup cost and monthly cost against $1,500 and $200, with prices dated and sourced
Every option says who edits, since the owner cannot
Every option has owner hours a week, risk and how success is measured
Interview versus solo is not assumed; both are costed

stages.name: Owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks the format, host and editing route. Ask why when a top option is passed over, and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options and the reasons are recorded
The chosen option fits the budget or the owner has accepted the difference

stages.name: Design the show and the first episodes
stages.goal: Write the show's promise, name options, description, cover art brief, trailer script, a plan for the launch episodes and the call to action in each.

checks.name: The promise names the listener and the problem in the owner's words
Each episode has one call to action to book a discovery call, at the start, middle and end
The plan reaches launch within eight weeks with a trailer and at least three episodes ready
No promise of promotion, pay rise or other results

stages.name: Prepare recording, editing and show notes
stages.goal: Make a recording checklist and run sheets for the launch episodes, an editing brief for the chosen route, and show notes for each episode.

checks.name: Every step is doable without editing skill, or says who does it
Includes a sound check for the owner's existing microphone before the first full recording
Show notes link the booking page and name the call to action

stages.name: Draft the listener page, tracking and announcements
stages.goal: Draft a simple show page with player and booking link, the Calendly question and tracked link, the email to the list and LinkedIn posts. Nothing is sent.

checks.name: A listener reaches the booking link in two clicks from the page and the show notes
A booking made from the show can be told apart from other bookings
Promotion to the existing audience is spread over several weeks
All messages are drafts for the owner to send

stages.name: Go live one approved action at a time
stages.goal: Register what each action should do, then with the owner's approval set up the Calendly question and link, upload the trailer and episodes, submit the feed, and send the announcements.

checks.name: Each action has its expected result written down before it goes live
The feed passes the apps' requirements and the show appears in the apps, or the wait is noted
A test booking from the show page records the source
What is live matches what the owner approved

stages.name: Count calls and downloads monthly
stages.goal: Each month, count calls from the podcast against 4, with downloads, completion and which episodes and calls to action brought bookings.

checks.name: Calls from the podcast are counted by the recorded source, and the unknown share is shown
Spend against $200 a month and the email unsubscribe rate are checked
A verdict on a format or call to action is given only after at least four episodes; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
The gap to 4 calls a month is shown each month

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each test, record what brought calls, propose rules with their scope, and plan the next season.

checks.name: Every test is closed with a verdict
Each rule says if it holds for this episode, this show or all shows

hypotheses.statement: A solo or coaching-style show with a discovery-call offer in every episode brings more calls than guest interviews.
hypotheses.test: Compare calls and booking-page visits by episode type over the first episodes.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Solo or coaching-style episodes bring more bookings per download.
hypotheses.refute_if: Interview episodes bring as many or more bookings.

hypotheses.statement: Listeners enjoy the show but do not book because the call to action is weak or hidden.
hypotheses.test: Booking-page visits and bookings per episode, with the call to action wording changed one at a time.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Downloads are healthy but visits and bookings are low.
hypotheses.refute_if: Visits are healthy and bookings follow.

hypotheses.statement: The existing 4,000 followers and 1,200 list are enough to start the show, but few will click through to listen.
hypotheses.test: Listens and visits from the first announcements, split by LinkedIn and email.
hypotheses.confirm_if: First-week listens are low relative to list size.

hypotheses.statement: Editing, not recording, is the bottleneck because the owner has no editing skill.
hypotheses.test: Hours and cost to get from raw audio to published episode for the first episodes.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Editing time or cost passes the budget or delays episodes.
hypotheses.refute_if: Editing fits the budget and schedule.

hypotheses.statement: Podcast calls will be undercounted because bookers are not asked how they found the owner.
hypotheses.test: Share of bookings with a recorded source, before and after the question is added.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Most bookings have no source today.
hypotheses.refute_if: Source is already recorded for most bookings.

hypotheses.statement: Four calls a month may not be the right measure if call-to-client conversion is unknown.
hypotheses.test: Ask the owner for call-to-client rate and fee after the baseline is known.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Rate and fee show 4 calls does not meet the owner's real business goal.
hypotheses.refute_if: 4 calls a month meets the goal.

measurement.window: Read calls monthly for six months after launch; judge each episode type or call to action after at least four episodes.
measurement.min_volume: No format verdict from fewer than four episodes or fewer than ten booking-page visits per variant; downloads alone never decide.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop and review if spend passes $200 a month, if unsubscribes from the owner's list rise above their normal level after announcements, or if a claim in an episode cannot be supported.
